name: NCHS Drug Poisoning Mortality by County (2021, model-based)
publisher: National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source_release_id: NCHS Drug Poisoning Mortality by County (rpvx-m2md, updated 2023-04-20; 2021 published)

geography_rules.county: County 5-digit FIPS (zero-padded from FIPS) joined exactly to TIGER/Line 2024 county equivalents. Every 2003–2021 row is staged; only 2021 is published. Connecticut's eight former counties (09001–09015) are staged as source_only (legacy_connecticut_county_code) and never crosswalked; other unmatched 5-digit county codes are staged as source_only (no_2024_boundary).

limitations: These are NCHS model-based estimates, not counts of recorded deaths. NCHS says that they may over- or under-estimate true rates, and that they may not match CDC WONDER.
Drug poisoning means ICD-10 underlying causes X40–X44, X60–X64, X85, and Y10–Y14 (all intents).
NCHS has not updated this file since 2023. Its latest year is 2021.
Connecticut values are for its former counties and are not shown on the 2024 planning-region boundaries.

measures.label: Drug poisoning death rate, model-based (per 100,000, age-adjusted)
measures.denominator: 100,000 population, all ages, age-adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population.
measures.official_definition: NCHS model-based age-adjusted drug poisoning death rate per 100,000 population (ICD-10 underlying causes X40–X44, X60–X64, X85, and Y10–Y14, all intents), estimated by hierarchical Bayesian modeling of NVSS mortality data.
measures.interpretation: Model-based county estimates with 95% intervals from NCHS's model, not counts of recorded deaths. They may over- or under-estimate true rates and may not match CDC WONDER. Latest year is 2021.
